name: Clark County

actions.title: Clark County Zoning Amendments for Data Center Siting in Industrial Zones
actions.summary: Clark County updated its zoning code to explicitly classify large-scale data centers as permitted uses in heavy industrial zones, streamlining permitting for hyperscale facilities in the Las Vegas metro area.

actions.title: (City of Las Vegas) Switch Data Center Campus Expansion Approval
actions.summary: The City of Las Vegas and Clark County approved expansion permits for Switch's Citadel Campus, one of the largest data center complexes in the world, allowing additional capacity and grid interconnection agreements with NV Energy.

actions.title: NV Energy Data Center Renewable Energy Rate Agreement
actions.summary: Clark County-based data center operators reached new utility agreements with NV Energy under Nevada's Portfolio Energy Credit system, committing hyperscale tenants to renewable energy procurement targets as a condition of expedited interconnection.

contextBlurb: Clark County is Nevada's primary data center hub, anchored by Switch's massive Citadel Campus and dozens of hyperscale colocation facilities near Las Vegas. The county faces growing pressure on its electrical grid and water supply as facilities expand, while also competing aggressively for economic development through tax abatements under Nevada's data center incentive program.

name: Washoe County

actions.title: (City of Reno) Reno Technology Park Data Center Siting Approvals
actions.summary: The City of Reno and Washoe County jointly approved siting and conditional use permits for multiple data center projects within the Reno Technology Park and adjacent industrial corridors, attracting operators seeking proximity to fiber infrastructure and lower land costs than Las Vegas.

actions.title: (City of Reno) Noise Ordinance Review for Data Center Cooling Equipment
actions.summary: Washoe County and Reno city planners initiated a review of noise ordinance thresholds following resident complaints about cooling tower and generator noise from data centers near residential neighborhoods in north Reno.

contextBlurb: Washoe County and the Reno-Sparks metro area have emerged as a fast-growing secondary data center market in Nevada, benefiting from favorable tax treatment, cheaper land, and robust fiber connectivity. Residential proximity to industrial zones has raised noise and water-use concerns as the cluster expands.

name: Storey County

actions.title: Storey County Industrial Tax Abatement Approvals for Tahoe-Reno Industrial Center Data Centers
actions.summary: Storey County commissioners approved Nevada sales and property tax abatements for new data center tenants at the Tahoe-Reno Industrial Center (TRIC), one of the world's largest industrial parks, under the state's data center tax incentive program requiring minimum capital investment thresholds.

actions.title: TRIC Data Center Grid Capacity Study and NV Energy Interconnection Queue
actions.summary: Storey County engaged with NV Energy and the Nevada Public Utilities Commission to assess grid capacity constraints at TRIC as multiple hyperscale data center projects queued for interconnection, raising concerns about transmission upgrades needed to serve the industrial park.

contextBlurb: Storey County is home to the Tahoe-Reno Industrial Center, a massive industrial park that has attracted Tesla, Google, and numerous data center operators. The county has aggressively used Nevada's tax abatement framework to recruit capital-intensive facilities, while grappling with significant electrical infrastructure demands from large-scale tenants.
